headline: Overland AI has launched Ibex, a self-driving ground vehicle that the US Marine Corps has picked for counter-drone work.
score_reason: Stays at pool 5: a real launch; performance and contract claims are the company's.
importance_line: What changed: a self-driving cargo vehicle is being put into US Marine Corps counter-drone work, which matters to Marine units and to the defense firms that supply them; the doubt: the performance figures and the first-contract claim come from the company, and no independent test is reported.
summary: Automotive World reports that Overland AI, which builds self-driving military vehicles, has launched Ibex, a ground vehicle built on the chassis of the Polaris MRZR (an off-road military vehicle) that carries 2,000 pounds and drives itself at over 35 mph. The US Marine Corps has selected Ibex for integration into its counter-drone system, and the company says the vehicle needs no remote control, figures that come from its own launch statement.
notes: Read via Automotive World. Chain: the company launch statement; the Axios exclusive named in the feed was blocked. machine_action true: the vehicle is described as driving itself; no footage read.
